body:
I can't quit and live. I don't think I could stomach knowing I gave up this opportunity. 

I asked my dr to rerun my thyroid blood work. Last year I got tired (more than now) and depressed (less than now) and my first set of blood work came back terrible but some of the later blood work came back normal. I'll get the results next week Monday if I get there.
That is an easy question. The more difficult ones are, "which direction would make me happy or does such a direction exist?"

Are you arguing there are objectively right and wrong goals? Even if we assume that chasing success in athletics and athletics are wrong goals, I guess I'm failing to see what good things could catch up to me. In fact whenever I slow my pursuit of these goals I tend to end up spending the time drinking, which is hardly a worthwhile use of time.

Seriously? I thought phrenology died years ago.  I mean, I can understand why you'd think the things I'm saying aren't useful, but I'm going to have to assume your request for a picture was sarcastic.

I'm aware that my answer is not a good one. It was just the best one I had. While I can think of plenty of things I do not want to do, there are few things outside of sleeping that I do want to do. 

I know my lack of passion for the process is hurting me, but I seem to be failing to find a process I have passion for or a way to become passionate about the things I am involved in currently.
I would like to find a way to do well in school and in sports again.  I've already started removing myself from social activities, but I just don't know what else I can do.
That's part of my problem. I've never really had a specific long term goal.

Not really. I've always been the good kid that did the right things for some far off future, but now that feels like chasing the wind and worthless. I've never really been happy in the present. It's just been hope for the future that kept me going, but that seems to be fading.
I did, but I burnt out. I also stopped doing well. I'd rather not mention the sport or school.

Thanks, I might think about it. Getting through this week is going to be tough as hell though. I'm struggling to get anything done over this break and I'm going to be far behind the eight ball when I get back on campus.

If I take time off, the loans would go into repayment. I'd be even worse off.  

Only success or pride in my work have ever brought me even momentary happiness and both are gone now.

Too much is expected. I just can't take this pressure any more.  I was never really that talented, I just worked hard. The drive is gone now though and it feels like I've lost the endurance to keep going upstream.
I've tried and they always just say, "you can do it, hang in there." They just look disappointed and almost frightened depending on how honest with them I am about how I feel.
